fcpr:ee4aaef5655f8aa4a29d59391a822f39889.rationale: The docstring only says this is "a variant" of the simultaneous double product property from Green's Problem 36, and the stated condition (each A i + B i has full size and is disjoint from every mixed sum A j + B k with j ≠ k) is a coherent rendering of such a variant with nothing checkably off.

The simultaneous double product property requires each diagonal sumset A i + B i to be disjoint from every other product A j + B k (in particular the sets A i + B i are pairwise disjoint), whereas the formal version constrains the mismatched sets A i + B j versus A j + B k only when i ≠ k, which neither implies nor is implied by the intended condition.

The sup over all pairwise-disjoint collections of blocks whose flips change the value of f, measured by cardinality, is exactly local block sensitivity (empty blocks are automatically excluded since flipping ∅ leaves f unchanged).

`Nat.count P n.succ` counts p < n+1, i.e. p ≤ n, satisfying the file's admissible-constellation predicate, matching the informal count (the factor 2 in the offsets is the file's own convention in IsPrimeConstellation).
Filtering Sym2 α by the symmetric predicate `dist u v = diam ∧ u ≠ v` and taking the card counts exactly the unordered pairs of distinct vertices at distance diam(G).

The disjointness guard `i ≠ k` omits exactly the essential cases `i = k ≠ j` (i.e. `A i + B j` vs `A j + B i`), so configurations like singletons a₁=0,a₂=1,b₁=0,b₂=1 satisfy the formal condition yet violate the simultaneous double product property.
The sup of cardinalities over collections of pairwise disjoint sensitive blocks faithfully renders local block sensitivity (empty blocks are automatically excluded since f(flip x ∅) = f x).
